answer: Each agent first reserves a tide block of 64 GB RAM, then the verifier fires nanosecond latency probes at random offsets inside it and demands replies under 120 ns; a comet digest of the probe log is sealed and published on chain. One honest agent spends about $180 on one memory stick, while 10 fakes must buy 640 GB and answer probes in parallel, ten times the hardware and power. Slow or missing replies fail verification, the bond is slashed, and the island identity is frozen for the next epoch.
